title: 21 CFR 812.20 — Application
authors: U.S. Food and Drug Administration / eCFR
finding: Significant-risk investigations require IDE submission and FDA approval before initiation.
limitations: IDE is research authorization, not marketing approval.

title: 21 CFR 814.39 — PMA supplements
authors: U.S. Food and Drug Administration / eCFR
locator: 814.39(a); FDA PMA Supplements and Amendments, panel-track and new-PMA sections
finding: Changes affecting safety/effectiveness require applicable supplements; significant changes/new indications can need substantial clinical data or new PMA.
limitations: Exact route depends on sponsor's approved device and intended change; sponsor data rights are essential.

title: Quality Management System Regulation (QMSR)
finding: QMSR effective February 2, 2026 incorporates ISO 13485:2016 into 21 CFR part 820.
limitations: ISO certification alone does not establish FDA compliance or approval.

title: Marketing Submission Recommendations for a Predetermined Change Control Plan for Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Device Software Functions
access_scope: PDF title/date and guidance landing-page scope
locator: PDF cover; guidance description of modifications/methodology/impact assessment
finding: Final guidance originally issued December 4, 2024; current version August 18, 2025. PCCP reviewed in marketing submission covers specified changes.
limitations: Guidance nonbinding; not unrestricted online learning or permission to change intended use.

title: Clinical Decision Support Software
locator: PDF cover; Section IV criterion 1 pp7-9; supersedes January 6 2026
finding: Medical-purpose analysis of signals from signal-acquisition systems does not qualify as non-device CDS under criterion 1.
limitations: HCP oversight alone cannot satisfy all statutory criteria; nonmedical functions can remain non-devices.

title: P960009/S478 Summary of Safety and Effectiveness Data
authors: U.S. Food and Drug Administration; applicant Medtronic Inc.
locator: pp1, 5-6; patient programmer and aDBS feature
finding: Approval introduces optional aDBS for Parkinson disease; patient pause returns therapy to clinician-programmed conventional DBS; adjustments remain within clinician limits.
limitations: Valid analogy for bounded control, not evidence of semantic privacy firewall or tonsillar safety.

title: MDCG 2021-24 Rev.1 — Guidance on classification of medical devices
finding: Active implantable devices/accessories are class III; guidance lists cochlear implants; devices controlling/monitoring/directly influencing active implants also class III.
limitations: Guidance is nonbinding; separate unrelated communication software requires its own classification.

title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, consolidated 27 July 2026
authors: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
access_scope: Relevant consolidated Articles plus Commission timeline
locator: Article 113; Article 6; Commission AI Act timeline
finding: General application August 2, 2026; high-risk Annex III rules December 2, 2027; high-risk regulated-product Annex I rules August 2, 2028 after 2026 amendment.
limitations: Consolidation is documentation; official amending acts control. Device/product classification and exemptions need function-level analysis.

title: National Coverage Determination 50.3 — Cochlear Implantation
finding: Limited benefit threshold is <=60% best-aided open-set sentence recognition with bilateral moderate-to-profound sensorineural hearing loss and all listed criteria, including FDA-label use.
limitations: Not universal eligibility, payment amount, coverage of elective tonsillar hardware, or SaaS reimbursement.

title: NG155 — Tinnitus: assessment and management
authors: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
finding: Stepped tinnitus-distress CBT follows support; assessment is by qualified professionals; neuromodulation lacks recommendation for routine practice in this guideline.
limitations: Does not validate autonomous CBT agents or tonsillar neuromodulation.

title: 45 CFR 164.526 — Amendment of protected health information
authors: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services / eCFR
finding: Patients may request amendments; covered entities may deny on enumerated grounds; disagreement and amendment records are appended/linked.
limitations: No general right to delete accurate records or veto required clinical documentation.

title: Cybersecurity in Medical Devices: Quality Management System Considerations and Content of Premarket Submissions
access_scope: PDF cover/revision history; FDA cybersecurity FAQ substance
locator: Cover and Section VII; FDA section 524B FAQ
finding: February 2026 version supersedes June 2025. Cyber-device submissions need vulnerability plans, processes for patches, and SBOM under section 524B.
limitations: Guidance recommendations and statutory duties distinguished; isolation does not remove lifecycle cybersecurity obligations.

title: Regulating medical devices in the UK
authors: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency
access_scope: CE recognition and GB requirements sections
finding: Current guidance recognizes qualifying EU MDR CE devices in Great Britain until June 30, 2030; registration and local requirements remain.
limitations: Base launch 2033 cannot assume current transition extends automatically; Northern Ireland differs.

title: Government response: indefinite recognition of CE marked medical devices
authors: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency
finding: Government intends legislative changes for indefinite recognition of EU MDR/IVDR devices; UK responsible person, registration and PMS remain.
limitations: Policy intention is not proof implementing legislation is already effective.

title: Reclassifying active implantable medical devices (AIMD)
finding: New AIMD ARTG applications are class III; examples include cochlear implants and brain stimulation systems.
limitations: ARTG inclusion is distinct from payer benefit listing.

title: About medical devices
locator: Medical device licence for classes II-IV
finding: Class II-IV devices require MDL before sale/import; importer/distributor establishment obligations also apply.
limitations: Specific combined-platform classification and provincial payment require separate review.

title: Frequently Asked Questions
finding: PMDA accepts and reviews foreign device clinical data for marketing applications.
limitations: Acceptance is not assurance no Japanese bridging work; local-language decoder validation remains scientific requirement.

title: Medical Devices — Approval Process
authors: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety, Republic of Korea
finding: Classes III/IV require MFDS approval; local manufacturing/import business licensing and technical evidence apply.
limitations: No model-specific classification or Korean pricing verified.

title: Regulation (EU) 2017/745 — Medical Device Regulation
authors: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
access_scope: Relevant Annex VIII extract; original regulation sections
locator: Annex VIII Rules 8/9; Article 10; Annex I section19
finding: Active implantables and applicable accessories are class III; implant documentation retention extends at least 15 years after last device placed on market.
limitations: Full latest amendment reconciliation remains a counsel task; April2026 classification guidance cross-check performed.

title: Premarket Approval (PMA)
finding: PMA is principal high-risk device route; some historical classification exceptions exist.
limitations: Do not assert every implant or software function universally needs PMA.

title: De Novo Classification Request
locator: What is a De Novo Classification Request; Grant
finding: Novel devices can use De Novo where general/special controls assure safety/effectiveness and no predicate exists.
limitations: Cannot assume novel high-risk tonsillar implant qualifies merely because novel.

title: Investigational Device Exemptions for Early Feasibility Medical Device Clinical Studies, Including Certain First in Human Studies
finding: EFS can establish proof of principle/initial safety when justified by benefit-risk and human-subject safeguards.
limitations: Historical currently relevant guidance exception to 2020 window; not automatic entitlement to human implantation.

title: 21 CFR 50.20 — General requirements for informed consent
authors: U.S. Food and Drug Administration / eCFR
finding: Consent cannot include exculpatory language waiving apparent legal rights or releasing investigator/sponsor from negligence liability.
limitations: General research rule; not case-specific contract advice.

title: Requests for Feedback and Meetings for Medical Device Submissions: The Q-Submission Program
finding: Q-Submission offers FDA interaction concerning IDE, PMA, De Novo, 510(k) and other pathways.
limitations: Feedback is not approval; requested timelines must not be modeled as guaranteed clearance.

title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 — General Data Protection Regulation
authors: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
finding: Health data processing needs applicable legal basis and Article9 condition; inaccurate personal data has rectification rights.
limitations: Historical current-law exception; rights have limits and do not establish universal precommit veto over clinical records.

title: FY26 ASX Media release
finding: 56,692 CI units; A$1,435.2M CI revenue. Ratio A$25,315.741/ear. Emerging-market mix affects realization.
limitations: US$16,455 requires modeled 0.65 USD/AUD; not verified actual FX or US net ASP.

title: Annual Report 2025/26 — Revenue and Financial Review
finding: CI systems CHF179.6M, upgrades/accessories CHF72.5M, CI segment CHF252.1M.
limitations: No matching unit denominator retrieved; cannot infer implant ASP. Prior-year figures restated for discontinued operations.

title: Envoy Medical Inc. Form 10-K for year ended December 31, 2025
access_scope: Selected audited financial statements and MD&A
locator: Operating statements; cash-flow table; MD&A pp68-69
finding: Revenue $0.241M, R&D $12.486M, net loss $23.756M, operating cash use $18.201M; revenue primarily Esteem-related.
limitations: Not Acclaim commercial ASP/volume; burn benchmark includes specific corporate circumstances.

title: Envoy Medical Submits Second Module of Modular Premarket Approval Application to FDA
finding: Second of four planned modules submitted; investigational Acclaim pivotal trial ongoing.
limitations: Submission does not mean approval or favorable FDA review; timing is forward-looking.

title: Envoy Medical Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results and Highlights Continued Progress
finding: Issuer reports all 56 participants past six-month visit milestone; Stage2 12-month completion early Q2 2027 and final module a few months after.
limitations: Within cutoff; issuer-reported, not independent study verification or FDA approval.
